True, NES dominated Japan and North America, but now there's this revisionists history to say that was also the case in Europe which is simply not true. Master System is pretty much to Europe what NES to the U.S. SNES dominated Japan (altho I'm not sure how soon that was after its release; PC-Engine took over for a bit once the Famicom was dying down but the Super-Famicom hadn't been released yet, altho that obviously didn't last for too long after Super Famicom's release), but America? No, there wasn't any "domination" honestly between it or the Genesis, but sales numbers at the time do show the Genesis had a slight lead from 1992 to the end of 1994, the biggest lead being in 1993 where it closer to a 65/45 split between it and Super NES in America. And while it did start outselling Genesis consistently after the release of DKC (an absolutely mediocre platformer I might add; DKC 2 was a much needed sequel), that wasn't such a hard thing to do when Sega themselves killed official support for Genesis in favor of Saturn. There's even some fault in the final numbers; no doubt SNES sold 49.1 million during its lifespan, but the 28 million famously quoted for Genesis only accounts for the American and possibly most of the European numbers. People tend to forget it was sold in other markets during its lifespan and when you include those markets the number creeps up closer to 40 million.

(*Should also mention that in Europe it was also close between MegaDrive and SNES, but iirc MegaDrive was #1 there over the course of the generation altho SNES did gain ground over the NES)
